[QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r7] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Awthān means idols.
[QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r8] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · أبو عبيدة | reports | Abu ʿUbayda distinguishes ṣanam, made of gold, silver, or copper, from wathan, made of plaster or stone.
[QURTUBI-FULL:29:16-19/r9] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · الجوهري | reports | Al-Jawhari says wathan means ṣanam and gives its plural as awthān.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | They worship idols and fabricate claims by calling them gods and alleging that they intercede with God.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | Alternatively, they make and carve the idols for the sake of falsehood; the phrase shows their practice is vile because it is fraud and untruth.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r6] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | Readings include form II, suggesting repeated making, and form V, suggesting affected or pretended making.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:29:16-17/r7] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | إفكًا may be a verbal noun like الكذب or an adjective meaning a creation laden with falsehood.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | This is a second argument against the idols: they cannot bring any benefit by providing sustenance.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | رزقًا may be an infinitive, meaning they cannot provide, or the thing provided; its indefinite form is general.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r3] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Seek all sustenance from God, since He owns it.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r4] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Worship and gratitude are means to obtain what you need and a way to acknowledge the blessings you have received.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r5] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | Alternatively, worship and gratitude prepare people to meet God.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:29:17-18/r6] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | reports | A reading has fatḥ on the tāʾ in ترجعون.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Awthān means idols.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | reports | Takhluqūn can mean that they lie and fabricate, or that they make things.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · أبو حذيفة والسلمى | reports | Abu Hudhayfa and al-Sulami read the form from khalaqa, conveying multiplying or making abundantly.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r4] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Afkan is also read; it is a verbal noun like lying or playing, while ifk is its shortened form, as kadhib and laʿib are shortened from their roots.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r5] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Their fabrication is calling idols gods and partners of God.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r6] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The idols cannot provide their worshippers any sustenance; God alone is the provider, so they should seek provision from Him.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r7] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | Worship and thank God for His blessings, preparing to meet Him, since you will return to Him.
[NASAFI-FULL:v3p253#5/r8] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · يعقوب | reports | Yaqub reads the t with fatḥa and the jīm with kasra, an active form meaning 'you return.'
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس | reports | Readings differ on tukhliquna and afkan; Ibn ʿAbbās says making idols is called falsehood because their makers falsely claim they are gods.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p347/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · مجاهد | reports | Mujāhid takes “fabricating falsehood” as inventing lies about idols and other matters; al-Zamakhsharī gives alternative grammatical analyses of afkan.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p348/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The verse argues that idols cannot provide sustenance, whether rizq means the act of provision or the provision itself; God owns all sustenance, so people should seek it from Him and give thanks.
[SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · العامة | reports | The common reading is from خلق; إفكا means fabricate a lie or carve idols.
[SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · علي بن أبي طالب وزيد بن علي والسلمي وقتادة | reports | Ali, Zayd ibn Ali, al-Sulami, and Qatada read with doubled ل, from تخلق; one ت is elided.
[SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · زيد بن علي | reports | Zayd ibn Ali is also reported with damma on ت and doubled ل.
[SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r4] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · ابن الزبير وفضيل بن زرقان | reports | Ibn al-Zubayr and Fudayl ibn Zarqan read أفكا as a verbal noun like lying.
[SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r5] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · الزمخشري | reports | Al-Zamakhshari allows إفك to be shortened from أفك or an adjective meaning false creation.
[SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r6] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | rejects | Al-Samin says an omitted noun is unnecessary if إفك is an adjective; it is needed only as a verbal noun.
[SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r7] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | رزقا is an accusative verbal noun governed by لا يملكون.
[SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r8] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · أصول الكوفيين | reports | Kufan analysis supplies لا يملكون أن يرزقوكم رزقا, with the infinitive clause as object.
[SAMIN-DURR:29:17/r9] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | Alternatively رزقا means that which is provided and is a direct object.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Abraham, the exemplar of the hanifs, calls his people to worship God alone, fear Him, seek provision only from Him, and thank Him as the sole giver of blessings; this brings good and repels harm in both lives.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · العوفي عن ابن عباس، مجاهد، السدي | reports | They say the people invented names for idols as gods, although the idols are created beings like their worshippers and can neither harm nor benefit.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عباس من رواية الوالبي، مجاهد، عكرمة، الحسن، قتادة | prefers | These authorities understand the phrase as making idols by carving them; Ibn Jarir also chooses this interpretation.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The phrase seek provision at God's presence forcefully restricts the request to Him, as in 1:5 and 66:11; no other being controls provision. | mentions 1:5, 66:11
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Ask God alone for provision; no one else owns anything to give.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p269/r7] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | Eat from God's provision, worship Him alone, and thank Him for His gifts; all will return to Him for judgment and recompense.
[BURHAN:v2p484/r4] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | When a present tense verb functions like a noun, it takes noun-like inflection, as in the sequence of commands to seek provision, worship, and give thanks.
[BURHAN:v2p49/r4] BURHAN, d. 794 · القاضي أبو بكر | reports | Al-Qāḍī Abū Bakr says revelation does not genuinely conflict with itself or reason; because God alone creates, تخلقون means “fabricate a lie” and Jesus’s خلق means “shape” clay. | mentions 6:102
[BURHAN:v3p152/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | reports | One reading takes الرزق in the earlier verse to mean one's share or allotment, so no ellipsis needs to be supplied. | mentions 29:17
[BURHAN:v3p322#2/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | Abraham's rebuke uses direct second-person forms—“you worship” and “you fabricate”—as an instance of shifting from third-person narration to address. | mentions 29:16, 29:17
[BURHAN:v4p99/r1] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | The rule that a second definite noun repeats the first applies when repetition is unintended; 29:17 deliberately repeats, as the prior repeated mention of Lord also illustrates. | mentions 29:17, 21:22
[BURHAN:v4p99/r2] BURHAN, d. 794 · غيره | reports | Another explanation says إله means “the worshipped”; a derived predicate denotes its attribute, so repeating ضارب with different objects does not repeat the same predicate in substance.
[BURHAN:v4p99/r6] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | reports | The source calls 29:17 a counterexample to the rule that a following definite noun is simply identical with the prior indefinite noun. | mentions 29:17
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p543/r14] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The phrase sets worship of God apart from worship of idols and describes God as incomparable, with no equal, second, or minister.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The plural idols scatter attention among many objects of worship; multiplicity entails division, in which there is no good.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Across its permutations, the root وثن co
<<part 2 ends; continues in part 3>>

<<29:17 notes, part 3 of 0..4>>
nveys increase and multiplicity, then division and softness or weakness; these senses are unfit for divinity.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Arabic derivatives illustrate abundance, dispersal, and weakness: wealth grows or increases, reports spread, and the fixed thing persists through lack of power to move.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · أبو منصور | reports | Abu Mansur distinguishes a wathn, a bodily object carved and set up for worship, from a sanam, an image without a body; al-Qazzaz transmits the distinction.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · بعضهم | reports | Some lexicographers instead treat wathn as synonymous with sanam.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r6] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · ابن عرفة | reports | Ibn Arafa, quoted through al-Harawi by Abd al-Haqq, calls any image made of plaster, stone, or similar material a wathn.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · أبو حاتم أحمد بن حمدان الرازي | reports | Abu Hatim defines a sanam as a stone statue and says a human image made on a wall is also called a wathn.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p544/r8] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · أبو حاتم أحمد بن حمدان الرازي | reports | Abu Hatim notes that Christians make images of Christ and Mary in their churches and prostrate to them.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r1] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The idols' multiplicity, division, and weakness make them unfit for divine rank, so the verse uses restriction as a reversal of the polytheists' claim that they are gods.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r10] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | All true authority belongs to God in this life, and people physically return after death for judgment; He can resurrect them effortlessly and reward or punish them in both abodes.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r2] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The present tense points to idol images being continually remade; people falsely call their handmade artifact a creator, a created thing a lord, and a servant an object of worship.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Ifk is something turned away from its proper truth: the fabricated objects are falsely declared divine.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Because humans always need benefit, the idols' inability to provide proves that all good belongs to God and that He alone deserves worship, refuting imagined power to benefit or harm.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The form of ابتغاء suggests exertion: God usually grants provision through effort, whether worship and reliance or ordinary worldly means; the idle should not merely indulge wishes and presume on God.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r6] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | All provision is with God; created things are ordered and interconnected so that removing any part would disorder the whole system.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r7] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Worship must be sincere and free of association; God alone merits it, rewards the worshipper, and punishes the one who turns away.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r8] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Do not let outward earning distract from worship, the true means; a sin may cause a servant to lose provision.
[BIQAI-FULL:v5p545/r9] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Give thanks to God alone for the blessings He has bestowed.
[DURR-FULL:v6p457/r1] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says the objects worshipped apart from God are idols.
[DURR-FULL:v6p457/r15] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · عاصم بن أبي النجود | reports | Asim reads the two letters of afkan lightly and reads awthānan mawaddatan in the accusative with tanwin, with baynakum accusative.
[DURR-FULL:v6p457/r16] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن عمر | reports | Asked about a sick person's praying on a staff, Ibn Umar rejects treating anything as an idol and says to pray standing if able, otherwise sitting, otherwise lying down.
[DURR-FULL:v6p457/r2] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · قتادة | reports | Qatada explains that the people fabricate falsehood by making idols.
[DURR-FULL:v6p457/r3] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · الحسن | reports | Al-Hasan glosses the phrase as carving idols.
[DURR-FULL:v6p457/r4] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as making falsehood.
[DURR-FULL:v6p457/r5] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid gives the same explanation as Ibn Abbas: they make falsehood.
[ITQAN:v2p325#3/r1] ITQAN, d. 911 · author | holds | In 29:17, تخلقون means 'make' or 'fashion,' and إفكا means 'a lie'.
[ITQAN:v3p80#2/r1] ITQAN, d. 911 · أبو إسحاق الإسفراييني | reports | If two verses cannot be reconciled, al-Isfarayini says to establish their chronology and treat the later as abrogating the earlier; if chronology is unknown, consensus on one practice identifies the abrogating verse. He says no unresolved case falls outside these conditions.
[ITQAN:v3p80#2/r3] ITQAN, d. 911 · الصيرفي | reports | Al-Sayrafi defines real contradiction as mutually opposed meanings in every respect; nothing in Qur'an or Sunna has that defect, while abrogation occurs at different times.
[ITQAN:v3p80#2/r4] ITQAN, d. 911 · القاضي أبو بكر | reports | Al-Qadi Abu Bakr denies conflict between Qur'an, reports, and reason: since only God truly creates, he reads تخلقون إفكا as 'you lie' and تخلق as 'you shape'. | mentions 39:62, 5:110
[BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Their objects of worship are manufactured images, with no quality beyond being fashioned statues.
[BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · بعضهم | reports | Some distinguish an idol (ṣanam), made from wood, gold, or silver in human form, from an image (wathan), made of stone and not in human form.
[BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r6] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · الراغب | reports | Al-Raghib says khalq is used of people for estimating or for lying; the source also applies it to fabrication with the tongue or by carving idols with the hand.
[BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r7] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Ifk is the worst kind of lie and is named for being turned away from its proper truth.
[BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r8] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | They commit a falsehood by calling idols gods and claiming they intercede for them with God; this proves their practice is fabricated and worthless.
[BURSEVI:v6p331#2/r9] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Malaka means to have power over something; the phrase from Moses means he had power over only himself and his brother (5:25). The indefinite rizq minimizes what idols can provide: nothing. | mentions 5:25
[BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | They should seek all provision from God, who alone can deliver it.
[BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Worship God alone and thank Him for His favors; worship carries requests to fulfillment, while gratitude secures blessings and draws further bounty.
[BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · ابن عطاء | reports | Ibn Ata says provision should be sought through obedience and turning toward worship.
[BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r4] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · سهل | reports | Sahl says to seek provision through reliance on God rather than earning, describing this as the way of ordinary people.
[BURSEVI:v6p331#3/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | They return only to God, through death and then resurrection, and should therefore do what Abraham commanded.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The restriction says they worship only idols, man-made statues with no quality beyond being fashioned, showing their religion is false in itself as well as against true religion.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r10] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | If رزقا is a verbal noun, it may be an absolute object by meaning or depend on an omitted verb, though Alusi considers the latter analysis strained.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r11] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعض الأجلة | reports | One eminent scholar says the indefinite رزقا intensifies the negation by suggesting even a little sustenance is beyond the idols; provision is singled out for its importance in creation.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r12] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | They should seek all provision from God; the repeated definite noun may be all-encompassing rather than identical to the earlier indefinite رزقا.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r13] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | They should worship God alone and thank Him for His blessings, using worship to seek their needs and gratitude to retain blessings and obtain more.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r14] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | The two imperatives may continue the preceding argument about provision or anticipate the return to God by preparing for the meeting through worship and thanks.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | One explanation is that they lie by calling the statues gods and claiming they intercede; another takes the phrase as making them for falsehood, with the lām marking an outcome rather than intent.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | A further possibility is that the wording is sarcastic.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعض الأفاضل | reports | Another scholar takes إفكا as the idols themselves, calling them falsehood by hyperbole, or as something turned from its proper state because people treat manufactured idols as creators.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r5] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · علي والسلمي وعون العقيلي وعبادة وابن أبي ليلى وزيد بن علي | reports | These readers pronounce the verb with an open initial tā and geminated lām; Ibn Mujahid traces it to تتخلقون, with one tā dropped, meaning to fabricate a lie emphatically.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r6] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن مجاهد | reports | Ibn Mujahid says this reading is also transmitted from Ibn al-Zubayr; some allow the form to carry the basic meaning فعل.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r7] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · زيد بن علي | reports | Zayd ibn Ali also has a reading from خلق with a geminated lām, describing repeated making in the sense of 
<<part 3 ends; continues in part 4>>

<<29:17 notes, part 4 of 0..4>>
lying and slander.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r8] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · ابن الزبير وفضيل بن زرقان | reports | Ibn al-Zubayr and Fudayl ibn Zarqan read إفكا with fatḥa on the hamza and kasra on fā, as a verbal noun or adjective modifying an omitted description of their fabrication.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p144#2/r9] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The idols are worthless because they cannot benefit their worshippers: they cannot provide any sustenance, whether رزقا means the act of providing or what is provided.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p145/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | The return clause may conclude everything Abraham said or its opening; the only return is to God at death and resurrection, so the people should obey, with the intervening case against idols as a parenthesis.
[ALUSI-FULL:v20p145/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | A reading with fatḥa on tā takes the verb from رجع, meaning that the people themselves return.
[ELMALILI:29:16-24/r1] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Awthan is the plural of wathan, any object worshipped, including stone images and fetishes; it is broader than asnam and includes standing stones and crosses.
[ELMALILI:29:16-24/r2] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | They fabricate falsehood by calling idols gods or intercessors; the idols are merely imagined entities.
[ELMALILI:29:16-24/r3] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | A portrait of Zayd contains no reality of the living Zayd, only an image of his mortal body; keeping the image and calling it Zayd is a lie.
[ELMALILI:29:16-24/r4] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Granting worship to transient imaginings is a grave slander.
[ELMALILI:29:16-24/r5] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | Idols cannot provide sustenance; without God's grace they cannot even help someone digest a morsel.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r1] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Exegetes often searched for occasions of revelation, events said to prompt a verse to explain a ruling, narrate an event, condemn it, or serve another purpose.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r10] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · الواحدي | reports | Al-Wahidi warns that people now invent occasions of revelation and fabricate lies; he says such claims require reports heard from eyewitnesses of revelation.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r2] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | rejects | Some exegetes overdid this search until readers could think every Quranic verse descended in response to a particular event, weakening confidence in their accounts.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Some verses themselves point to their occasion, and some occasions are established through transmission rather than a narrator’s conjecture; ignoring the topic entirely also risks misunderstanding.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r4] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Ibn Ashur discusses occasions of revelation in his introduction to assess them carefully during exegesis and avoid repeating the methodological discussion.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | reports | He excuses early authors who collected many occasions because enthusiasm for a new subject naturally led them to expand their compilations.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | rejects | He does not excuse leading exegetes who accepted weak reports without marking their reliability, creating the false impression that revelation depended on triggering events.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The Quran guides people toward communal well-being and does not need events to occur before it can reveal legislation.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r8] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | reports | Most scholars say an occasion of revelation does not restrict a verse’s general wording; a deviant minority claimed that it does.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p46/r9] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The usul principle is that general wording governs rather than the specific occasion, though some reports try to specify general wording or restrict an unrestricted expression and can distort interpretation.
[TABATABAI:29:14-17/r12] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | أوثان is the plural of وثن, meaning an idol.
[TABATABAI:29:14-17/r13] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | إفك is something turned away from its true direction, whether a statement or an act.
[TABATABAI:29:14-17/r14] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Calling the idols merely idols exposes the falsehood of their worship and makes clear that true worship belongs to God alone; the indefinite plural belittles them as empty claims to divinity.
[TABATABAI:29:17-19/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | They fabricate falsehood by naming idols gods and worshiping them; a God worthy of worship exists, but He is the one God, not the idols.
[TABATABAI:29:17-19/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | People worship idols as intermediaries to attract benefit and provision, but idols cannot provide it: God created both people and their provision, and ownership follows creation.
